note.text: Public finance concerns government revenue, expenditure and financing. Taxes and non-tax receipts can provide revenue; borrowing finances a gap but is not counted as revenue in this stated model. Expenditure purchases services or assets and makes transfers under the applicable budget classification. Revenue minus expenditure gives a surplus if positive, a deficit if negative and balance if equal. A deficit is a flow during a period; public debt is a stock at a date. Fiscal choices differ from central-bank monetary policy.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish public revenue, expenditure and financing and calculate a stated budget balance. Builds on: government/central-bank distinctions and financial records. Leads to: later taxation, public spending and budget-policy analysis.

sections.heading: Follow the local case
sections.text: Original simplified public budget: tax receipts {12000}, non-tax receipts {3000} and expenditure {18000} CFA francs. Revenue is {12000+3000}; balance is {12000+3000-18000}. Borrowing that finances the gap does not turn the deficit into tax revenue. These tiny invented amounts teach a relationship, not a real Cameroon government budget or tax rule.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Use the period and classification stated. Add revenue categories, subtract expenditure and interpret the sign. Keep financing and revenue separate, and distinguish an annual deficit from total debt. Real budgets require more detailed classifications than this introductory model.

questions.prompt: An invented public-budget model has tax revenue {t} CFA francs, non-tax revenue {n} and expenditure {e}. Borrowing is financing, excluded from revenue here. Calculate revenue minus expenditure.

misconceptions.explain: Expenditure alone is not the revenue-minus-expenditure balance.
Spending is subtracted in this balance rather than added as revenue.

solution: Balance = {t+n} − {e} = {answer} CFA francs. A negative result is a deficit in this stated model.
